english.html: are worthy of great praise. But taking up again our track and the path of our discourse: the men who have thus their shameful parts cut off, because they are deprived not only of the generative power, but also of being able to approach a woman <sup class="mk" data-key="z">z</sup>, cannot in any way contract marriage <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>. Secret and hidden impotence is that which proceeds from bewitchment and sorcery <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>, by which a man is sometimes rendered impotent toward all women, one excepted (she, perhaps, who has given him the morsel or worked the spell), sometimes toward one only, and able to have to do with all the others <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>: a thing certainly little credible, if by innumerable experiences we had not some certainty of it. Now such an enchantment is not perpetual, because it can be removed, either by an interval of time, or by a contrary bewitchment, or even (and very often in our Gascony) by him who has made and ordained it <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>; for, as the Philosophers say, in human acts everything that can be bound can be unbound and dissolved <sup class="mk" data-key="e">e</sup>. Whence it must undoubtedly be believed that such an impediment does not suffice to undo a marriage already contracted <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>, unless it be after three years from the day of the nuptials, from which time, if the marriage has not been able to be consummated by carnal work, the law presumes the impediment to be perpetual <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>; true it is that some have further doubted whether this impotence was a sufficient cause to dissolve the marriage, seeing that God permits separation only for lechery and adultery <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. A great and true reason, where the marriage should once have been consummated by carnal cohabitation <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>; but before the consummation it is without difficulty lawful for the wife (whose husband has not the power of a man) to leave him and take another <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>. Reconciler's ruling at 10x (pages/strips/p043/body-6.jpg, second line, x about 180-300 of 1699): it is an exclamation-mark sort — a heavy wedge, widest at ascender height, tapering downward to a point just above the baseline, with a separate round dot beneath it on the baseline. It is not a turned i (a turned i would be a stem of even width with a serif at one end and a dot at the other, and this stroke has no serif and tapers steadily), and it is not foul or damaged type (the impression is crisp on all edges). A wrong sort pulled from the case, one of the roughly one-per-page wrong sorts in this print. Transcribed as '!' with §1 spacing (no space before, one after). placement: the margin column is crowded (42 note lines against 40 body lines), so notes z, a, b, c, d and e begin one to five lines above their markers; f, g, h, i and k sit level with or one line below theirs. beside_line values are the nearest body line by vertical centre and are approximate to about half a line.

the line-end sign after 'il' is a short raised slanted stroke, the margin italic's hyphen ('il|lud').
